<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915244_theRebbe_950" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915244_theRebbe_950__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar for Shabbos Vayeitzei, 10 Kislev 5722.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos of Parshas Vayeitzei,</t>
    <t s="2">10 Kislev, Maamar 3,</t>
    <t s="3">5722*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that war is called "krav" from the term for closeness, as the Divine soul must draw near to the animal soul to influence it during prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Baal HaGeulah explains in his maamar beginning with this phrase</t>
    <t s="2">(printed in his book Shaarei Teshuvah),</t>
    <t s="3">that the reason war is called by the term "krav," from the language of closeness (kiruv)</t>
    <t s="4">(even though war is the opposite of closeness),</t>
    <t s="5">is,</t>
    <t s="6">that the matter of war is that each of the two combatants wants to defeat the other and subdue him so that he will be included within him,</t>
    <t s="7">and in order to effect this—that he fights against him so that he will be included within him—</t>
    <t s="8">it is specifically through the closeness that he draws near to him,</t>
    <t s="9">"krav" from the language of closeness.</t>
    <t s="10">And similarly, regarding the war between the Divine soul and the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="11">the primary war is during the time of prayer</t>
    <t s="12">(the time of prayer is the time of battle),</t>
    <t s="13">so that the service</t>
    <t s="14">(prayer)</t>
    <t s="15">of the Divine soul will affect the animal soul so that it becomes included in the Divine soul</t>
    <t s="16">[meaning that even the animal soul will have love for G-d,</t>
    <t s="17">"with all your heart, with both your inclinations"],</t>
    <t s="18">it is through the Divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="19">that the contemplation of the Divine soul is in such matters and in such a manner that even the animal soul can grasp.</t>
    <t s="20">However, when prayer is from the soul itself,</t>
    <t s="21">it does not affect the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="22">as explained in the maamar.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the refinement of the animal soul through the Divine soul clothing in it is a matter of war, whereas "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to redemption through the revelation of a supernal light that nullifies the animal soul's desires without war.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the refinement of the animal soul through the Divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="2">is a matter of war,</t>
    <t s="3">as above.</t>
    <t s="4">For the matter of war is,</t>
    <t s="5">that there is an opponent and one must wage war against him.</t>
    <t s="6">And the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that the redemption of the Divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is not in a manner of war,</t>
    <t s="7">but rather,</t>
    <t s="8">that through the revelation of a supernal light, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,</t>
    <t s="9">so that there is no need for war at all.</t>
    <t s="10">And as explained in many places,</t>
    <t s="11">and also in the aforementioned maamar,</t>
    <t s="12">regarding the refinement through engaging in Torah study,</t>
    <t s="13">which is not in a path of war</t>
    <t s="14">(meaning that there is an opponent but one defeats him through war,</t>
    <t s="15">but rather)</t>
    <t s="16">that through the revelation of the light of Torah, it is the nullification of evil in its very essence.</t>
    <t s="17">.</t>
    <t s="18">And similarly regarding prayer,</t>
    <t s="19">that through the love that is above reason and intellect, from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,</t>
    <t s="20">and the redemption of the Divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is in a manner of peace,</t>
    <t s="21">"He redeemed my soul in peace."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
